steps.content: Beneath your feet, the ground speaks: hard, cold, rough with the texture of years untouched. Dilapidated walls lean within arm's reach, their facades long stripped away to reveal stonework sealed for ages.

Decay varies from structure to structure, yet every collapsed doorframe hangs frozen mid-swing as if pushed open in desperate haste. Every shattered window faces the same direction. Through those hollow gaps, you see the quiet debris of ordinary lives.
If this is Maria City, where the Perishing Star fell, then the disaster struck in an instant. The people here tried to flee the moment it happened. But...
You cross a fallen doorframe and step inside. Dimness swallows you. The air is stagnant, thick with dust that hangs suspended, as though even time refuses to let it settle.
Tables and chairs keep their positions, patient as mourners. But the tableware has abandoned them, scattered across the floor in fragments.
On the wall, a damaged clock points to a frozen hour. It is not alone. On tables, inside cabinets, tucked into corners—every timepiece you find has stopped. All at once. All at the same moment.
The street constricts with each step, buildings leaning inward like conspirators ready to seal their trap. Then, without warning, the space exhales, opening wide again.

The layout shifts without reason, but the stench only deepens: rotting, briny, suffocating. Drag marks score the ground in every direction. They seem chaotic at first, but on closer look, they all point the same way.
You attempt to stop, but the <color=#fb9259>silence</color> has already stopped you first. No footsteps. No breath. Only the damp kiss of mist against your skin.
The moment you sense it, the ruins ahead begin to move.
Shadows writhe within them, contorting into shapes that almost resemble human forms. Hollow faces twist in what should be screams. But there is only silence.
Then the wave takes form. They surge together, a torrent of forgotten things, and rush forward to swallow you whole.
